source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact original XML verse substrings including all written/read and other notes, not normalized reconstructions.
source.public_versification_note: Public Joshua 9–17 and Hebrew source references align one to one. All 256 original source records are bound exactly once.

key_decisions.decision: Keeps the LORD as the continuing grammatical subject; notes that later verbs may be understood of Israel or Joshua.
Preserves explicit divine agency, great stones identified as hail, and the comparison of deaths.
Keeps the public address, cosmic imagery and poetic parallel without importing a physical explanation.
Preserves the poem, vengeance, cited book, and approximate duration without scientific harmonization.
Keeps the unique-day claim and divine listening/fighting as the narrator’s conclusion.
Preserves both the totalizing defeat and stated survivors, rather than deleting their tension.
Preserves the tongue image with a short idiom note and retains the Makkedah camp location.
Preserves public humiliation and command/fulfillment repetition without turning the action into a metaphor only.
Preserves killing before hanging, five trees and the duration of corpse display.
Retains all victims, the herem claim, no-survivor formula and Jericho comparison.
Clarifies the agents without softening the exhaustive killing and repeated king comparison.
Retains the second-day detail, every-person scope and prior-city comparison.
Keeps the named relief force and total defeat without claiming capture of Gezer here.
Keeps both same-day references and the shift from collective capture to Joshua’s destruction.
Keeps dependent towns, full human scope and repeated destruction, without harmonizing the earlier death of Hebron’s king.
Retains every repeated comparison and distinguishes capture, killing, and herem language.
Keeps all four terrain zones and the narrator’s exhaustive destruction and divine-command claim.
